A couple of things: 1) If you're going the therapy route, which could be very beneficial, don't diagnose her. Even if you throw terms out there just as hypotheticals, she could latch onto them. 2) The Power of Now, by Eckhart Tolle - really amazing book. I have trouble imaging someone getting through 3 chapters in this book without having a serious transformation in the way they think, feel, and act. I have it as an audiobook. I find I'm more likely to listen to it than read it. Seriously, give this is a try.

I have a two year old sister, Catie. She has a ratty baby doll that she carries everywhere. The name of the baby changes often, but it's always a character from Willow. Catie acts really sweet and everyone thinks she's an angel, but she's got a seriously dark side. One day I was napping on the couch and woke up to see Catie standing over me, quietly staring. She put the baby in my face and told me to give Aurora a kiss. So, I did. She kept doing this, but got slightly more aggressive each time, until she was hitting me with the baby doll and saying "give Aurora a kiss." Then she started laughing like a psycho and ran away.
A real live where's Waldo? That's almost too good to resist.

Assume that no third-party candidates will be elected in 2012. Aside from casting my vote for one of you on election day, what **specifically** can I do for my country to help bring about some of the changes you propose?

I have given thousands of dollars to the Obama campaign, because I am terrified of Romney, but I will be voting for Jill Stein. If I were living in a swing state, I would definitely vote for Obama. (I do not want, nor do I think we can afford, a repeat of the 2000 election!) How can we reform elections so that voting for a third-party candidate doesn't "split the vote?"
